newsitem.title: CHINA: China says laws in '97 to regulate futures markets.
newsitem.headline: China says laws in '97 to regulate futures markets.

text.p: Chinese authorities will adopt more laws and regulations in 1997 to regulate the futures markets amid difficulties in defining current speculation on the markets, the Securities Daily said on Wednesday.
The Securities Commission has urged the quick passage of rules to define manipulation of the futures markets and punishments, the newspaper said.
Management rules on futures brokerages would also be passed as well as provisional rules to govern futures exchanges, it said. Both are expected to take effect in 1997, it said.
Other complementary regulations were being drafted, it said, but gave no details.
"The publication of these regulatory laws will be greatly beneficial to the development of the healthy development of the futures markets," the newspaper said.
With the return of Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty, China will speed up the international links of its markets as well as greater inter-regional cooperation, it said.
In 1997, prices of production materials and staple agricultural products will tend to increase but the possibility of sharp rises was unlikely, it said.
